title: Divide & Bind Your Attention for Improved Generative Semantic Nursing
role: Training-free cross-attention latent optimisation (total-variation attendance plus JSD binding) that names token competition in cross-attention as the source of hybrid animals; a no-box fix aimed at presence
enters_evidence: argument with visualised maps on one prompt: overlapping single peaks let one object token take over the other's region, giving a missing object or a dog-turtle hybrid (Fig. 3); no measurement across prompts
changes: gradient step on z_t minimising -min_s TV(A_s) plus lambda * JSD(attribute map || object map) on 16x16 cross-attention maps, steps 50 to 25 of 50 (first half), lambda 1 with attributes else 0
training: nothing trained; needs object and attribute token indices, by hand or extracted by GPT-3 with in-context examples; no boxes, masks or reference image
model: SD (version, resolution and sampler not printed), 50 steps; no transfer claim; no SDXL
similar_subjects: Animal-Animal (66 prompts), SD: TIFA 0-1 higher better +32% over SD vs A&E +31% (SD about 0.70, read from bars); text-text CLIP 0.81 vs A&E 0.80, SD 0.77; CLIP min-object 0.246 vs A&E 0.249, SD 0.220; paper calls it on-par with A&E
which_pairs: not measured per pair; argues token competition grows with prompt complexity and a single attention peak can be taken over by the competing token
when: not measured; cites other work that semantics are set in the initial denoising steps and optimises steps 50 to 25 of 50 for that reason
cost: about 17 s per image against 13 s for plain SD on a V100 at 50 steps (about 1.3x); one extra backward and forward per optimised step
headline: TIFA (0-1 VQA accuracy, higher better) on Multi-Object prompts with SD: 0.785 against Attend-and-Excite 0.755 and SD 0.647
suggests: (inferred) supports testing cross-attention overlap as the predictor and logging each subject map's total variation; as a fix on CO3 it needs no boxes but on animal-pair prompts only its presence term runs, which does not target part borrowing between two present bodies

quotes.text: The single excitation of one object token may overlap with others, leading to the suppression of one object by another
or to hybrid objects, exhibiting features of both semantic classes (e.g., mixed dog-turtle in Fig. 3)
Since cross-attention layers are the only interaction between the text prompt and the diffusion model
a single excitation can be easily taken over by the other competitor token, leading to missing objects in the final image.
As the complexity of prompts increases, token competition intensifies.
We maximize the total variation of the attention map to prompt multiple, spatially distinct attention excitations.
we propose a Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD) based binding loss to explicitly align the distribution between excitation of each object and its attributes
The optimization is operated on the attention map at 16 × 16 resolution
the update is only performed from t = T to t = tend , where T = 50 and tend = 25 in all experiments.

quotes.text: The weight of binding loss λ = 1, if the attribute information is provided. Otherwise, λ = 0, i.e., using only the attendance loss.
